scope: Full resolved dependency graph, including development and optional dependencies; advisory records are not unique CVEs or confirmed runtime exposures.

advisories.title: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects
Glob: AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal
image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
image-size: ICNS parser allows denial of service through an infinite loop
KaTeX: Existing prototype pollution can bypass trust restrictions
minimatch has potential denial of service via globparts amplification
Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections

deepmerge.status: Locally mitigated; npm still reports the unchanged package version.
deepmerge.verification: 12 regression checks across CommonJS and UMD; clean offline install replay under Node confirms all three prototype-poisoning shapes are blocked.

image-size.status: Locally mitigated by upstream-derived backport; npm still reports unchanged package versions.
image-size.verification: 5 passing actual Metro-chain parser and Buffer/file/callback checks; malformed inputs run in memory/time-capped workers. Original package failed three cases.

katex.status: Locally mitigated by upstream-derived backport; npm still reports unchanged package versions.
katex.verification: 6 passing runtime-variant checks across both versions/CommonJS/ESM/minified browser bundles: own explicit trust preserved, inherited settings/macros rejected, ordinary rendering hashes unchanged. CSS/fonts untouched.

glob.status: Locally mitigated by upstream-derived backports; npm still reports unchanged package versions. Glob 7 is outside the advisory range.
glob.verification: 36 clean-install checks across versions 10.5.0/11.1.0/13.0.6, CommonJS/ESM, async and sync streams: cancellation stops filesystem reads, queued callbacks settle, normal and paused/resumed walks work.

minimatch.status: Described optimization-level-2 amplification path locally mitigated in modern versions. Legacy 3.1.5/5.1.9 lack this optimizer path; this is not a claim that arbitrary old patterns have no resource cost. npm still reports unchanged versions.
minimatch.verification: 8 clean-install worker checks across legacy callable APIs and modern CommonJS/ESM variants: bounded expansion, large-set dedupe cutoff, ordinary matching. Modern workers are memory/time capped.

zod.status: PARTIAL: bounded-collection backports plus approved application input envelopes mitigate inspected entry points. npm still flags v3; dependency-internal/uninspected consumers are not established globally safe.
zod.verification: 41 clean-install tests across Zod 3.25.76 and Zod 4.6.7 embedded v3 CommonJS/ESM plus the actual v3 JSON-schema adapter; bounded collections skip child allocation/async dispatch, valid transforms/defaults and normal errors remain compatible. Unbounded arrays deliberately retain full-error behavior.
zod.remainingDecision: Input-limit approach approved and implemented. Remaining high record is retained conservatively for dependency-internal/uninspected parsing paths; full removal requires supported upstream/consumer migration and separate verification.

followUpInvestigation.finding: No behavior-preserving global resource ceiling exists for the current unbounded full-error contract. Supported v4 boolean APIs do not replace transformed parsing and do not bound genuinely async dispatch.
followUpInvestigation.decisionNeeded: Approve workload-specific input envelopes and/or bounded diagnostic/work semantics; preserve the existing 25 MiB attachment allowance.
followUpInvestigation.deploymentLimits: not verified; not counted as mitigation
followUpInvestigation.decisionStatus: Resolved: user approved workload-specific input envelopes; see inputLimitRemediation.

combinedCleanInstall.cache: Initially empty .fresh-bun-cache; official registry downloads; frozen lock; lifecycle scripts disabled.

unmitigatedAuditScope: Conservative unresolved dependency-level subset. Application ingress mitigations are recorded separately; they do not suppress npm records or establish safety for every internal dependency parser.

inputLimitRemediation.status: Implemented and verified locally; user approved input envelopes.
